title: BNCI 2019-001 Motor Imagery dataset for Spinal Cord Injury patients
description: EEG recordings from 10 persons with cervical spinal cord injury performing attempted arm and hand movements: hand open, palmar grasp, lateral grasp, pronation and supination. The data show that low-frequency time-domain EEG (movement-related cortical potentials) carries information that supports offline five-class decoding. An online proof-of-concept for self-paced movement detection is also included. The aim is to support neuroprosthetic control for upper limb and hand grasp restoration.
methods_description: 61-channel EEG plus 3 EOG channels were recorded at 256 Hz with g.tec active electrodes (10-5 montage, left earlobe reference, AFF2h ground). Participants attempted or executed cued movements over 9 runs, with 72 trials per class (360 trials in total). Preprocessing included bandpass and notch filtering, ICA-based artifact removal, common average referencing and trial rejection. Decoding used shrinkage LDA in 10x10-fold cross-validation.
